claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: For a proposed L, scanning every L-square proves feasibility, while one sum-greater-than-k witness for each length l>L proves that no larger length is feasible. This is necessary and sufficient despite nonmonotonicity; lengths below L are irrelevant. For L=0, feasibility is vacuous and witnesses for all positive lengths prove the optimum is zero. A 2D prefix table costs O(mn), the L-scan uses at most mn queries, and at most q=min(m,n) witnesses are checked, giving O(mn) arithmetic/word operations. Exact exhaustive checks covered 63,756 signed matrix/threshold cases, including L=0 and rectangular matrices.
claims.search_method: Independent necessity-and-sufficiency proof, boundary-case analysis, and exhaustive exact-integer enumeration.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending through all lengths returns the first feasible length, hence the exact maximum without assuming monotonicity. After orienting dimensions so m>=n=q and writing d=q-L, length q-t has (m-q+t+1)(t+1) placements. Thus the probes through L are bounded by the stated sum, which is O((m-q+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3); adding prefix preprocessing gives the claimed bound. Since d<=q<=m, this is O(mnq), and for constant d preprocessing dominates at O(mn). When L=0, the t=q term is indeed merely an unused upper-bound term. Exact exhaustive checks matched brute-force optima and verified the probe bound in all 63,756 tested cases.
claims.search_method: Re-derived descending-search correctness and placement-count bounds, then compared against brute force using exact integers.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: In the proposed n-by-n family, an even-length first-row interval sums to zero, while an odd-length interval sums to either 1 or -1 and the interval starting in column one sums to 1. Squares not meeting the first row sum to zero. Hence F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l, so feasibility at k=0 alternates for every consecutive length. For [[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]] at k=1, the two side-2 sums are exactly 1 and 4, while F_1=2. Continuing forward after reducing from side 2 to side 1 can therefore miss the earlier entry 2 and return 1 although the true answer is 0. Exact checks verified the family through n=32 and the concrete greedy witness.
claims.witness: k=1 and A=[[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]]: side-2 sums are [1,4], F_1=2, and the true optimum is 0; the alternating family has first row 1,-1,1,-1,... and all other entries zero at k=0.
claims.search_method: Symbolically evaluated all window sums and independently reproduced both constructions with exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, every l-square sum is XY for independently selectable length-l window sums X and Y. A bilinear function on [min X,max X] times [min Y,max Y] attains its maximum at one of the four corners, all of which correspond to actual row/column-window pairs. The pivot identity pA_ij=A_icA_rj is necessary and sufficient for nonzero rank at most one; products of pivot-representation window sums are divisible by p because they aggregate integer entries. Taking the maximum after exact division handles p<0. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, the sum is l(X+Y), maximized independently by max X and max Y, and the stated recognition identity is necessary and sufficient. Prefix-window extrema cost O(m+n) per length, and q(m+n)<=2mn. Exact checks covered 23,125 signed multiplicative cases, 6,656 signed additive cases, and exhaustive 2-by-2 recognition tests.
claims.search_method: Proved both separations and recognition identities algebraically; exhaustively compared their extrema formulas with brute-force square sums using arbitrary-precision integers.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For t in [0,2N-2], a side B-t first-row window has start s in [0,t] and value p_{B-(t-s)}-p_s. When i=s and j=t-s are valid, overwriting gives C+x_i+y_j. If i>=N, p_s=H and the value is at most C+W-H=-1; if j>=N, the endpoint is -H and the value is at most W-H<0. Valid values are at least C-2W=1, while squares starting below the supported row have sum zero. Therefore F_{B-t}=C+c_t exactly. These are consecutive descending side lengths: if a coefficient passes c_t<=K, the least such t gives the global largest feasible side B-t; if none passes, no encoded side is feasible. The arbitrary middle prefix values cannot occur at these endpoints. Exact checks covered 16,278 signed vector pairs, two distinct middle assignments per exhaustive pair, all valid and invalid endpoints, threshold behavior, and additional large-magnitude cases.
claims.witness: The symbolic endpoint mapping s=i and B-(t-s)=B-j realizes C+x_i+y_j; the H and -H sentinels make every invalid endpoint window negative.
claims.search_method: Checked all index ranges and sentinel inequalities algebraically, then exhaustively reconstructed the one-row matrices with exact integer prefix differences.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: For the 1-by-1 equality input a=k=2^(B-1), the answer is 1. Changing any one of its B-1 lower zero bits to one preserves the B-bit input length but changes the answer to 0. On the equality input, an exact algorithm must either inspect every such position or perform an operation whose bit cost accounts for them; otherwise an uninspected single-bit alternative is indistinguishable. Thus the worst-case cost is Omega(B), excluding a bit-time O(mn)=O(1) bound independent of B. This is only an input-length obstruction and does not exclude O(mn) unit-cost arithmetic/word operations. The checker confirmed 32,640 such single-bit alternatives for B=2 through 256.
claims.witness: For every B>=2, use a=k=2^(B-1); replacing a by 2^(B-1)+2^r for any 0<=r<B-1 changes the answer while changing exactly one lower bit.
claims.search_method: Applied an explicit-binary indistinguishability/adversary argument and enumerated its finite instances with exact integers.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a general O(mn)-time algorithm for all integer matrices, including signed entries, or a matching impossibility result under a stated standard assumption. The draft establishes neither substantive endpoint. Its linear verifier, O(mn min(m,n)) search, nonmonotonicity examples, O(mn) separable special cases, and max-plus embedding are correct and material but incomplete. The unbounded-bit Omega(B) result is a generic input-reading obstruction, not an impossibility result for the usual bounded-word or unit-cost endpoint. The final writeup explicitly makes this distinction and says the main endpoint remains unresolved. Therefore PARTIAL is accurate, neither overstated nor understated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and iteration-5 draft JSON; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior run, verification report, or other solution.
Read the exact target independently of the draft claim list and separately assessed target coverage and claimed_resolution.
Re-derived the certificate characterization, descending-search correctness, output-sensitive placement bound, and all L=0 and rectangular-orientation cases.
Checked the alternating family and the 2-by-3 no-revisit counterexample symbolically and computationally.
Proved the rank-one and additive-separability extrema and recognition formulas, including zero pivots, negative pivots, and exact divisibility.
Verified every valid and invalid endpoint range in the one-row max-plus embedding and its threshold-to-largest-length correspondence.
Re-derived the explicit-binary Omega(B) adversary while separating it from the bounded-word endpoint.

Ran the persisted checker successfully with arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic and no floating-point decisions: 63,756 general cases, 33 alternation/counterexample cases, 23,125 rank-one cases, 6,656 additive cases, 16,278 max-plus vector pairs, and 32,640 bit alternatives passed.
